recipes.name: Easy Slow Cooker Lasagna
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) container POLLY-O Original Ricotta Cheese
1 (7 ounce) package KRAFT 2% Milk Shredded Mozzarella Cheese, divided
0.25 cup KRAFT Grated Parmesan Cheese, divided

steps.text: Combine ricotta cheese, 1 ½ cups mozzarella cheese, 2 tablespoons Parmesan cheese, parsley, and egg in a bowl; set aside.
Brown meat in a large skillet; drain. Stir in spaghetti sauce and water.

Spoon 1 cup meat sauce into a slow cooker; top with ½ noodles (broken to fit) and ½ ricotta mixture. Add 2 cups meat sauce; top with remaining ½ noodles (broken to fit), remaining ½ ricotta mixture, and remaining meat sauce. Cover slow cooker with lid.
Cook on Low until liquid is absorbed, 4 to 6 hours. Sprinkle with remaining mozzarella cheese and remaining Parmesan cheese; let stand, covered, until melted, about 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Slow Cooker Lasagna
raw_recipe.description: This easy homemade slow cooker lasagna recipe from Kraft is assembled in your slow cooker, and simmers for hours without the fussy preparation and baking.

review.reviewBody: This was so easy and the finishing taste was very good. I basically doubled it. I threw in a little balsamic vinegar in the cheese mix. Used some ground beef and Italian sausage. The finished lasagna was about 4-inches thick and came out of the slow cooker nicely in a decent piece. Try it, you'll like it.

I just made this for the 3rd time. I've substituted broccoli and spinach for the ground beef this time. I also use more noodles, about 8 to 10 but I'm using a 6.5 qt slow cooker. 
I love how simple and easy this is so it fits well with my busy schedule.
Another variation I just tried: I mixed all the ingredients except the noodles in the slow cooker. Then I took about 10 noodles and broke them up and mixed them in with everything else. When it was done I spread some more mozzarella cheese on top, covered, and let it sit for about 10 minutes. I probably should have used a little more sauce and/or water but it was still good.

Made this for Thanksgiving dinner at work. Everyone loved it!! It was gone in no time. I would suggest leaving out the water and use more lasagna noodles. I used 1 lb of ground Italian sausage and 1 lb of ground chuck.

I make my own layers including some ninja veggies (ninja veggies = sneak up on you without you noticing) 
 I also use breakfast turkey sausage that comes in the 1# tube packages - it's lower in fat and also has some good seasoning in the meat which adds to the overall flavor
I use sauce with basil or add in my own sweet basil in the layers, preferably the Trader Joes one if i go by a Joes
First thing i do is start soaking in warm water the lasagna noodles in a large nonstick frying pan so the cook all the way, no matter what kind of lasagna noodles you use.

I loved this recipe, and plan on using it again, adding different vegetables or meat. It's great when you're using your oven for something else, or for warmer months, when you don't want your oven on. The only think I changed was adding an onion and some diced garlic cloves before I added the beef to the skillet, and I added some oregano too. I cooked it for 4 1/2 hours, and it was a bit scorched in one corner, so next time I would stop at 4 hours.

We loved this dinner! I didn't have ricotta cheese so I substituted cottage cheese and I added veggies....mushrooms, onions, garlic and peppers with the ground beef. I also had the no cook noodles on hand so I used them. I doubled the recipe in a large slow cooker. It made tons :)

Delicious and easy. I doubled the recipe and put in large oval crockpot. I did add some Italian seasonings and garlic to the meat and cheese mixture for more flavor. It turned out great. It was just a touch dry but I believe I cooked it too long due to my poor timing. Easy fix with a little extra sauce over the top.

Easy, and pretty tasty. Great to make in the summer, when you don't want the whole house heated up by the oven.
Changes:
-Use Classico Basil Tomato Pasta sauce (or equivalent) instead of spaghetti sauce
-Use whole wheat lasagna noodles
-Use 2 teaspoons dried parsley (instead of fresh)
-Use cottage cheese instead of Ricotta 
-Added Frozen, chopped spinach to cottage cheese mixture (about 1/2 to 3/4 cup)
-Omitted the 1 egg
-Lasagna seemed cooked after about 3 or 3.5 hrs on low, in slow cooker

This is very easy and good. Some of the reviews state that this dish lacks flavor. I seasoned the meat with onion powder, garlic powder, italian herb mix( basil and oregano), salt and pepper. I added the spagetti sauce and water. When I tasted it, I found the water had diluted the flavor of the sauce. I added about 1,5 teaspoons of italian herb mix to the sauce. I followed the rest of the recipe exactly . I cooked it for 6 hours. I took off the lid for the last hour to help some of the liquid evaporate. When I served this there was a small amount of liquid at the bottom, but it didn't detract from the dish. We all loved it!

This was very good! I mixed Ragu Garden Chunky and Sauteed Onion Sauces together with the meat. Used more ricotta as my family loves it and used dry italian seasoning in the ricotta mix. It was much better the next day as a left over so I recommend making it a day in advance. We will definitely make this again without a doubt.

I used Italian sausage in place of ground beef. Added some granulated garlic to cheese mixture. Sautéed 1/2 of a large onion and added to sauce, in addition to some chili flakes and dried oregano. It was delicious! Will definitely make again!
I’m not sure what I did wrong but this turned out more like a lasagna soup than an actual lasagna. It tasted ok, but it wasn’t anything like a traditional lasagna.

Family thought it was so great. Instead of destroying a set of lasagna noodles, I used Fusillis. Also, used my homemade bolognese sauce and a pinch of nutmeg and an extra egg to my cheese mixture. I love my slow cooker, "oven" made meals in the summer.
I love this recipe! But I did make changes! Instead of adding water I added a can of stewed tomatoes. And I added all kinds of italian herbs.

Love this recipe! Lots of room for changes to personal preferences! I found that using the breakfast seasoned ground turkey meat was awesome! I used the oven bake noodles and soak them in water as I'm doing the rest of my prep & then they come out perfect. Everybody loves it - we call it lagonena cause there's never leftovers for long!
I'm not sure if I did something wrong but it was pretty soupy, which I didn't like. My son did though. I might try it again and leave out or reduce the water.

I've made this three times now this year and I just finished getting it in my slow cooker for tonight's dinner. It comes out really well, with the noodles perfectly cooked, and it's delicious! I will never make Lasagna any other way again. Thanks for the recipe!
This was delicious and so easy!! Thank you
